2Wind
0 = right ahead, 090 = starboard beam, 180 = astern, 270 = port beam. Uses course & speed from step 1.
True wind: –
From the sea you get TRUE wind – no need to factor out ship's speed. Deep water, steady wind only: shallow water, wind against current, heavy rain or ice, a sudden wind change and swell can all make the sea look rougher or calmer than the wind.
3Visibility & weather
When visibility is not the same in all directions, estimate it in the direction of least visibility.

W1 W2: –
Past and present weather together should describe the weather as completely as possible. If the weather changed completely, past weather describes the weather before the present weather. The app sends the highest ticked code as W1 and the next as W2.

Nh counts low cloud only. If there is no low cloud, count the middle cloud. If there is only high cloud (cirrus), Nh is 0.

    Sending

    NOAA default: Shipobs@noaa.gov, subject "Weather Observation". If your ship email system doesn't open from the Email button, use Copy and paste into a new mail.

    How to use – SOFast WX V01.20

    1. Fill in Setup once (call sign, barometer height & correction).
    2. First obs: fill the top bar (position) and steps 1–8. The coded message builds live.
    3. Check the warnings, click any group to double-check it, then Copy & save (Ctrl+Enter) and paste into your email to NOAA.
    4. Next obs with no big weather change: date and hour follow the device clock (Auto time). Click DR (Alt+D) for the dead-reckoning position from the last saved obs, or type the position, then Copy & save. Readings you don't touch carry over.
    5. Picking a date or hour by hand switches Auto time off. Click Auto time to turn it back on.

    Works with no internet. On iPhone: open in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen. On Windows: open the file in Chrome or Edge.

    This app is a helper, not official software. Check your output against TurboWin+ or the NOAA Observing Handbook No. 1, and confirm your ship is registered with your Port Meteorological Officer before sending.

    NOAA procedure notes (Guide to Sea State, Wind, and Clouds)

    • Wind: 98 kn or less is coded in actual knots as ff in Nddff. 99 kn or more: ff = 99 and the speed goes in an extra 00fff group. The app does this for you.
    • No anemometer: estimate the Beaufort force from the sea (Wind → Beaufort). This gives true wind; don't factor out ship's speed. Keep a close, continuous watch on the sea and be aware of any swell.
    • Sea photos are for deep water and steady wind. Shallow water makes waves steeper (wind overestimated). Heavy rain and floating ice damp the sea. Wind against tide or current makes higher, rougher seas; with the current, smaller. The sea lags behind a sudden wind change. Swell makes more whitecaps.
    • Sea vs swell: sea is made by the local wind now or recently; swell has travelled from elsewhere, with lower, rounder crests, regular trains and a longer period.
    • Clouds are coded in 8NhCLCMCH. Low: base below 2 km. Middle: 2–8 km. High: 3–18 km. Cumulus and cumulonimbus can reach all levels. Types blend into each other, so watch how the sky develops.
    • Full coding rules: Ships Code Card or NWS Observing Handbook No. 1.

    Message layout

    BBXXShip report header, then call sign
    YYGGiwDay, hour (UTC), wind unit indicator (4 = knots measured, 3 = knots estimated)
    99LaLaLaLatitude in tenths of degrees
    QcLoLoLoLoQuadrant (1 NE, 3 SE, 5 SW, 7 NW) and longitude in tenths
    iRiXhVVPrecip group omitted (4), weather group included (1) / not observed (3), cloud base h, visibility VV
    NddffTotal cloud, true wind direction (tens of °), speed (kn). 00fff added if 99 kn or more
    1sTTTAir temp (s: 0 positive, 1 negative; tenths °C)
    2sTdTdTdDew point
    4PPPPMSL pressure, tenths hPa, thousands dropped
    5apppTendency type and 3-hr change
    7wwW1W2Present and past weather
    8NhCLCMCHCloud amount and types
    222DsvsSection 2: ship's course (Ds) and speed (vs)
    0sTwTwTwSea temp with method
    2PwPwHwHwWind waves: period (s), height (half metres)
    3ddddSwell directions (tens of °)
    4/5PPHHPrimary / secondary swell period and height
    6IsEsEsRsIce accretion
    8sTbTbTbWet bulb (s: 0 positive, 1 negative, 2 iced)
